claim:
Let \(R_\lambda^2=(\mathbb R^2,N_\lambda)\), where \(1<\lambda\le\sqrt2\) and
\[
N_\lambda(u,v)=\max\{\lambda|u|,\sqrt{u^2+v^2}\}.
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\), write \(a\perp_D^\varepsilon b\) when
\[
N_\lambda(a+t b)\ge\sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2}\,N_\lambda(a)
\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).
\]
Then the least \(\varepsilon\) such that
\[
x\perp_B y\Longrightarrow y\perp_D^\varepsilon x
\qquad(x,y\in R_\lambda^2)
\]
is
\[
\varepsilon_D(R_\lambda^2)=\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_{R_\lambda^2}\\x\perp_B y}}
\inf_{t\in\mathbb R}N_\lambda(y+t x)=\frac1\lambda.
\]
Equality is attained at
\[
x=\left(\frac1\lambda,\sqrt{1-\lambda^{-2}}\right),
\qquad y=(0,-1),
\]
and at their images under the sign symmetries.

correctness.rationale: The unit ball is a Euclidean disk clipped by the strip |u|<=1/lambda. Circular arcs, vertical edges, and corners are exhaustive. Smooth strata have forced Birkhoff directions; each corner uses the full norming-functional segment. The quotient-distance formula computes every reverse line distance exactly. Circular pairs are strictly above 1/lambda, edge pairs are at least 1/lambda, and a corner/vertical pair attains 1/lambda.
risks: The argument depends on beta<=alpha, equivalently lambda<=sqrt(2); it is not extended past that phase boundary.

value.rationale: Modified-Dragomir symmetry quantitatively measures the failure of Birkhoff--James orthogonality to be symmetric, while the general finite-dimensional theorem supplies existence but not sharp parameters. The Banaś--Frączek spaces are a classical one-parameter family with a genuine geometric phase boundary at lambda=sqrt(2). The result determines a full natural parameter interval and identifies the extremal mechanism at the clipped-disk corner, rather than computing an arbitrary isolated slice.
risks: The second regime remains open in this finding, so the result is a one-phase profile rather than a complete all-lambda theorem.
